Despite a well marked course, Barratt and Cliff Roffey went off course round by the Ponds and eventually Walker and Barratt ran in together.

Barratt of Ealing was an easy winner in 43.17, followed by Olney 44.13, and Ingles another minute back, third Peter Bagnall ran well to be 4th in 45.42, but he had no backing from the rest who included Short 9th, Gebbett 12th, Abbott 13th, L.

John Thresher and John Davies produced fine efforts to beat Barratt of Ealing in the mile clocking 4:24.4 and 4:25.7 respectively. As can be seen already, conditions were certainly not conducive to fast times.
On the same day Bill Kerr finished 4th in the Middx. 3miles behind Taylor, Briault, and Barratt.

Halton, Geoff finished second to Briault in the Sefton Brancker Trophy match between the Civil Service, Middlesex and the R.A.F In leading the Civil Service team to victory Geoff easily beat Price, Pugh, Presland, Barratt, Cooper, Ellis, Entwistle, Mellor, Lindsell and Holts.
Barratt and Bivens filled the first two places for the home club, with Laurie O'Hara 3rd. Ealing & Southa ll won the team race from ourselves and Verlea, 46/64/80.
